observation.visible_scene: A wall-mounted rustic lamp: a rectangular wooden bracket fixed to a light-colored wall, with a thick rope looped over a horizontal wooden arm, from which hangs a spherical open-weave rattan/bamboo shade containing a glowing warm bulb. A diagonal lattice shadow falls on the wall to the left, and a vertical door/window frame edge is visible at the right. The bulb is lit throughout.
visible_changes: Overall image brightness/exposure ramps up rapidly from a near-dark first frame to a fully lit, normal-exposure scene by roughly the 4th-5th frame, then remains steady for the rest of the excerpt (consistent with a fade-in or camera auto-exposure settling, not with the bulb being switched on, since the bulb glow is present from frame 1).

A slight, slow frame-wide translation/scale shift occurs across the clip (the bracket, shade, wall shadow and right-side frame edge all move together by a small amount), indicating minor camera drift/zoom rather than independent motion of the lamp.
The lamp assembly (shade, rope, bracket) keeps a constant relative geometry and orientation; no swinging, rotation, or deformation of the shade is discernible.
The bulb's glow and the cast lattice shadow pattern remain essentially unchanged once exposure stabilizes.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the brightness ramp (fade-in, auto-exposure adjustment, or a dimming circuit) is not shown.
Whether any lamp sway or camera motion began before frame 1 or continues after the last frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether the small frame-wide shift is camera pan, dolly/zoom, or handheld jitter cannot be resolved from these samples.
The exact timing mechanism of the exposure increase (editing fade vs. sensor adjustment) is not determinable.
